questions.q: Name the three basic components found inside a standard torchlight that allow it to function.
questions.a: The three components are the battery, the bulb, and the switch. If a student mentions the "casing" or "lens," they are focusing on structural parts rather than the electrical circuit components, indicating a need to differentiate between appearance and function.

questions.q: If you take the battery out of your torchlight, the bulb will not light up even if the switch is in the "ON" position. Why?
questions.a: The battery is the source of electrical energy; without it, there is no energy to power the bulb. A student who says "the switch is broken" misses the fundamental role of the battery as the energy provider in the circuit.

questions.q: A torchlight has a switch. If the switch is "OFF," how would you describe the status of the electrical circuit?
questions.a: The circuit is "broken" or "incomplete," meaning electricity cannot flow. A student who says "the circuit is still working" fails to understand that a circuit must be a continuous loop to function.

questions.q: If a torchlight is "ON" but the bulb is not glowing, what is one possible reason related to the circuit components?
questions.a: The bulb might be fused (broken filament) or the battery might be dead. This shows the student can analyze why a closed circuit might still fail to produce light due to a faulty component.

questions.q: Is a torchlight with the switch in the "OFF" position considered a "complete" circuit? Justify your answer.
questions.a: No, it is an "open" or "broken" circuit because the switch creates a gap that prevents electricity from returning to the battery. Justifying this requires understanding that the "OFF" position is a physical disconnection.

questions.q: Imagine you are building a simple torch model. You have a bulb and a battery, but no switch. How could you manually turn your "torch" on and off?
questions.a: You could manually connect and disconnect one of the wires attached to the battery. This demonstrates that a switch is simply a mechanical tool for making or breaking a connection.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A torchlight is a portable electrical system that generates light by creating a complete path—called a circuit—for ______ to flow from a battery to a bulb.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever wondered why your ______ doesn't stay on all the time, even when the battery is inside?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify the three essential components (battery, bulb, and switch) and explain how the movement of the switch completes or breaks the path of electricity to turn the light on or off.
